:::{#thm-normalizing-constant-formula}
#### The normalizing constant makes the density integrate to 1

If $g$ is a [kernel of a density](#def-kernel) $f$,
its [normalizing constant](#def-normalizing-constant) is

$$c = \frac{1}{\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} g(x)\,dx}.$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}

::: proof

A [density](#def-pdf) integrates to 1 over the whole line, so

$$
\ba
1
&= \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f(x)\,dx
&& \text{(a density integrates to 1)} \\
&= \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} c\, g(x)\,dx
&& \text{(@def-normalizing-constant)} \\
&= c \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} g(x)\,dx.
&& \text{(constant factor out of the integral)}
\ea
$$

Dividing by $\int g(x)\,dx$ gives the formula.

:::

:::
